transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because I’m having trouble staying with things I need to focus on. Like, I’ll sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document, meaning to get through it, and then… ten minutes later I realize I’ve just been looking at the same page and thinking about other things. I’m not really taking it in.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself moving around when you need to stay still, like tapping your feet, fidgeting, or feeling like you can’t sit still for long?
Not really, no. I mean, I might shift in my chair like anyone, but I haven’t noticed feeling like I can’t sit still or needing to move around all the time.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have off days, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed or stopped enjoying things, not really.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or finishing things you start?

Yes, I do. Mostly with finishing the last bit. Like if my department chair gives me a few things after a meeting, I’ll start one and get most of it done, but then something small at the end—sending the file or updating the calendar—just doesn’t happen unless I’m reminded.
Do you often lose things like paperwork, pens, or other items you need to complete tasks, even if you know you had them not long ago?

Yeah… that does happen. I’m always looking around for things I need for the day—classroom keys, lesson notes, my USB drive. Even stuff for refereeing, like the whistle or cards. I’ll be sure I just had it in my hand a few minutes ago, and then it’s gone.
Do you find yourself getting easily frustrated or upset over small things, or feeling like even minor criticisms or setbacks affect you more strongly than they should?
I’m not sure. I mean, everyone gets annoyed sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed it being a big pattern or anything.
Looking back, did you have similar issues with focusing or finishing tasks when you were a child, like in school or while doing homework?

Yeah… I think so. My school reports used to say things like I was “bright but careless,” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was watching me closely. My parents would find old worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d just forgotten to hand in.
Do these difficulties with focus and organization happen in different parts of your life, like at work, at home, or when you’re out with friends or family?

Yeah… it’s not just one place. At work it’s gotten bad enough that my department chair put me on a support plan because I keep missing follow-through on things. And at home… my wife’s started handling the bills and reminders more, because she doesn’t really trust me to keep track of them.
Do you also find it hard to stay focused or organized when you're out with friends or family, or does it seem to be more of an issue at work and at home?

Mostly work and home, I think. Work’s been… serious enough that my department chair put me on a support plan. And at home my wife’s taken over a lot of the bills and reminders, because I haven’t been reliable with keeping track of them. With friends or family, I’m not as sure.
Do you ever find it hard to stay focused or organized during social activities, like when you’re out with friends, at a family gathering, or during a hobby or sport you enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I notice it most with things like marking essays or reading curriculum stuff. I’ll sit down intending to get through it, and then ten minutes later I’m still on the same page, not really taking it in, thinking about other things. Social stuff… I’m less sure, honestly.
Can you think of a time when you noticed trouble focusing or staying organized during a social activity, like a gathering or while participating in a hobby or sport you enjoy?

I’m not sure about social things, honestly. The clearest example is more when I’m trying to read or mark work… like I’ll sit down with essays or a curriculum document, meaning to get through it, and then realize I’ve spent ten minutes on the same page and haven’t really taken it in. My mind’s just been somewhere else.
Can you recall if you've ever had trouble staying focused or keeping things organized while you're out with friends or at a family gathering, even for a short time?
I can’t really think of a clear example, no. I mean, maybe I zone out a bit sometimes, but nothing that stands out to me like the work stuff does.
Have you noticed any times when you had trouble focusing or staying organized while doing something you enjoy, like a hobby, sport, or during leisure time?

Not really with hobbies, no… or at least nothing I can pin down. The main thing I notice is when I sit down with essays or a curriculum document, meaning to get through it, and then I realize I’ve been on the same page for ages, thinking about other things and not really taking it in.

Can you think of a time when you had trouble staying focused or found yourself losing track of things during a leisure activity, like watching a movie, reading for fun, or playing a game, even for a little while?

Not so much with films or games, no. The thing I keep coming back to is work reading — essays, curriculum stuff. I’ll sit down meaning to get through it, and then after a bit realise I’ve just been staring at the same page, thinking about other things, and not really taking any of it in.

Can you think of a time when you had trouble staying focused or found yourself losing track of things while doing something you weren’t required to do—like reading for fun, watching a show, or working on a hobby, even for a little while?

Not really for things like shows or hobbies, no. The example I keep thinking of is more work-related… I’ll sit down with essays or a curriculum document, meaning to get through it, and within maybe ten minutes I realise I’m still on the same page, thinking about other things and not really taking it in.

When you're working on tasks that don’t require much mental effort, like watching a video or chatting with a friend, do you still find your mind drifting or losing track of things, or does that mostly happen when you're doing something that feels tedious or mentally demanding?

Mostly when it’s tedious or takes effort, I think. Like… the reason I came in is that I can sit down with essays or a curriculum document fully intending to get through it, and ten minutes later I’m still on the same page, thinking about three other things and not really taking it in. Videos or chatting don’t stand out in the same way.

Can you think of any situation—work, home, or leisure—where you're required to maintain focus for a longer period, even something small, where you didn’t have trouble staying on task or keeping track of what you were doing?

I mean… the main one is still the school work. If I’m marking a stack of essays or reading a curriculum document, I can sit down meaning to just get on with it, and then pretty quickly realise I’ve been on the same page for ages, not really taking it in. My mind’s just gone elsewhere.
